resources.string: No reference range for your age or parameters
This measurement was edited manually; related metrics may not have been recalculated.
Height for this older measurement was restored from the account owner’s profile.
The assessment uses a height of %1$s cm, the profile’s current sex, and an age of %2$d years on the measurement date.
This metric is estimated from bioelectrical impedance and profile data. It is intended for tracking trends, is not a diagnosis, and may vary with measurement conditions.
Do not use bioelectrical impedance during pregnancy, with a pacemaker, dialysis, implanted medical equipment, or severe edema. Consult a doctor if you are unsure.
Categories are consumer reference interpretations, not diagnoses or medical advice.
Xiaomi Legacy — reconstructed Mi Fit scales
Schutz et al., 2002 — FMI P5/P95 percentiles
Additional non-interactive reference: Chumlea — total body water models.
Additional non-interactive reference: Janssen et al., 2000 — skeletal muscle mass equation.
Additional non-interactive reference: NIAMS — how estimated bone mass differs from BMD and T-score.
Additional non-interactive reference: ESPEN/GLIM — clinical FFMI context, not used as a Weigh Together rating scale.
Body mass measured directly by the scale.
Weight boundaries are calculated from saved height using Xiaomi Legacy BMI thresholds. The weight category therefore always matches the BMI category.
Saved height and weight. Impedance is not used.
Weight alone does not determine health. No category is shown below age 20 or outside the scale’s domain.
Electrical resistance between the scale’s electrodes. It is used as an input for body composition calculations.
The value is read from the scale’s BLE packet in ohms and is not recalculated separately.
Foot contact, electrode arrangement, frequency, body geometry, hydration, skin temperature, and measurement conditions.
The value itself is not a health indicator. Scales from different BIA devices are not interchangeable; there is no universal reference range.
The relationship between weight and height. BMI does not show body composition and is not a diagnosis.
Weight in kilograms is divided by saved height in meters squared. Categories use Xiaomi Legacy thresholds of 18.5 / 25 / 28 / 32.
These are not the current WHO clinical classes. No category is shown below age 20.
Estimated proportion of fat tissue in total body mass.
A Xiaomi-compatible BIA formula uses weight, impedance, height, age, and sex. The category uses the age- and sex-specific Xiaomi Legacy table.
Current profile sex, age on the measurement date, saved height, and BIA conditions.
This is an algorithmic estimate, not a direct measurement of fat tissue. Consistent trends under similar conditions are more useful.
Estimated mass of fat tissue in kilograms.
Mass = weight × body fat %. The reference category uses FMI: fat mass / height², compared with the Schutz P5/P95 percentiles.
Estimated body fat, weight, saved height, current sex, and age.
P5–P95 are population percentiles for adults in Geneva, while “Normal” is a Weigh Together product interpretation. The scale is unavailable below age 18 and above age 98.
Estimated proportion of total body water. This is not the amount of water consumed.
A Xiaomi-compatible formula derives the metric from estimated body composition; the category uses a sex-specific Xiaomi Legacy scale.
Current sex, body composition, hydration, and measurement conditions.
It does not replace an assessment for dehydration or edema.
Estimated total body water mass in kilograms.
Body size and estimated water percentage.
The absolute amount is naturally higher in a larger person and does not indicate hydration by itself. There is no compatible universal kilogram scale.
Weigh Together subtracts estimated fat mass and bone mass from weight. The category uses Xiaomi Legacy thresholds by sex and height.
Current sex, saved height, weight, and all BIA inputs.
The value depends on the algorithm and does not measure muscle strength or function.
Estimated mass of the muscles that move the body.
The Janssen equation uses height, impedance, sex, and age. For the category, mass is divided by weight, converted to a percentage, rounded to 0.1%%, and compared with the OMRON table.
Current sex and age, saved height, weight, and impedance.

Janssen used whole-body BIA; Xiaomi uses foot-to-foot BIA. Applying OMRON categories is a consumer interpretation. It does not assess strength or diagnose sarcopenia. The reference range is unavailable below age 18 and above age 80.
Estimated mineral component of the bones.
A Xiaomi-compatible formula uses sex and a BIA estimate of the lean component. The category depends on sex and weight.
Current sex, weight, and the BIA calculation.
This is not bone mineral density, a BMD/T-score, or an osteoporosis screening test.
Estimated proportion of protein components in the body.
An internal Xiaomi-compatible formula uses muscle mass, weight, and water. Xiaomi Legacy thresholds are 16% and 20%.
All muscle mass and water inputs.
It does not show protein intake, blood protein, or diet quality.
Estimated mass of protein components from Weigh Together’s internal formula.
Estimated muscle, water, protein, and weight.
This is not a validated total body protein mass, a blood protein test, or a dietary target. There is no compatible kilogram scale.
Estimated index of fat around internal organs.
A Xiaomi-compatible regression uses sex, age, height, and weight. Xiaomi Legacy thresholds are 10 and 15.
Current sex and age, saved height, and weight.
This is a dimensionless algorithmic scale, not a mass, percentage, waist circumference, or CT/MRI area.
Estimated energy the body uses at rest over one day.
Weigh Together uses a formula based on sex, age, height, and weight. The Xiaomi Legacy reference threshold equals weight multiplied by an age- and sex-specific coefficient.
Current sex and age, saved height, and weight.
This is not a daily calorie target, dietary advice, or a direct calorimetry measurement.
An algorithm-specific indicator based on body composition.
A Xiaomi-compatible regression uses height, weight, age, impedance, and sex. Following the TANITA pattern, the category compares the result with the profile’s current age on the measurement date.
Current sex and date of birth, saved height, weight, and impedance.
It does not determine biological age and is not used for diagnosis. The reference range is available only from age 18 through 99.
An internal Xiaomi Legacy estimate used by the body composition formula.
The regression uses height, weight, impedance, and age, then clamps the result to the algorithm’s technical limit.
Current age, saved height, weight, and impedance.
This field does not strictly correspond to clinical fat-free mass. External FFMI thresholds do not apply to it; the technical clamp is not a reference range.
